title: Cycle 26: SQLite-backed rate limiting + route audit for local-auth endpoints
summary: Added durable sliding-window rate limiting and structured route audit events to BrowserOS local-auth endpoints. The limiter reuses the existing SQLite token-family store, so counters survive restarts without adding dependencies. Rate-limit violations return 429 with Retry-After; auth routes now record token issuance, refresh attempts, reuse, and not-found events with the caller socket address.
weak_spots: No route-level audit events for token issuance or refresh usage
No socket-address tracking on auth endpoints
Generic 403 for every local-auth failure with no differential signal
competitors: OWASP ASVS 5.0 V6.1.1 / V6.3.1 — rate limiting on auth endpoints
OWASP Bot Management Cheat Sheet — sliding-window, per-IP buckets, generic 429

variants.A: In-memory per-IP rate limiter (fast, counts reset on restart)
variants.B: SQLite-backed sliding-window rate limiter + durable route audit (implemented)
variants.C: Redis-backed distributed rate limiter (multi-instance, external deps)

lessons: Sliding-window rate limiting is the right algorithm for auth endpoints because it prevents burst abuse at window boundaries.
Reusing the existing SQLite store for rate-limit counters keeps the dependency graph unchanged and makes counters durable across restarts.
Single-row upserts per IP are simpler and sufficient for a single-server loopback surface; no need for a separate window table.
Route-level audit events should be recorded near the HTTP boundary, separate from family-lifecycle audit, to preserve operator signals.
Tests that construct stores with default paths can silently write to the production database; always use :memory: in unit tests.
When auth requirements change, agent-route tests that POST without the required header are the first to break; keep test helpers explicit.
